recipes.name: Spiced Quinoa
ingredients_raw: 1 (14 ounce) can garbanzo beans, drained and rinsed
0.5 cup raisins, soaked in hot water and drained

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook and stir onion and garlic in hot oil until onion is softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in stock, quinoa, curry powder, salt, pepper, cumin, and cinnamon; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until quinoa is tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir beans, pine nuts, and raisins into cooked quinoa. Serve warm or cold.

raw_recipe.headline: Spiced Quinoa
raw_recipe.description: This quinoa is flavored with aromatic Mediterranean and Indian spices for a quick and delicious side dish.

review.reviewBody: I found this when searching for recipes using chick peas (had leftovers from a batch cooked in crockpot). Sounded interesting so gave it a try. Glad I did! I'll make it again. I did increase the spices quite a bit after tasting finished dish...didn't measure, just "palmed it". Have to admit that the aroma while cooking had me wondering if I'd made a mistake...the combination of spices smelled kinda strange to me, did again when opening leftovers, but I do like the flavor. It's one of those flavors that I found growing on me more with each bite. Increasing the spices considerably didn't drastically change the flavor as much as I thought it would...even though I could feel the beginning of heat in my mouth. Sent leftovers with daughter for school lunch today...waiting to see what she thinks. I used raisins and think that, like others, they add a definite depth to the flavor that's important (and I usually don't care for raisins much). Didn't have any pine nuts so couldn't add those, but will definitely next time...and there will be a next time. Thanks for the recipe!! I've been looking to increase our use of quinoa. UPDATE I changed the rating to a 5. My daughter really likes this for her school lunch. I've made it a few more times and have added pine nuts...they do add another layer of flavor/texture that we like. This is going into our regular rotation making sure to cook for leftovers.

Substituted almonds (toasted and then pulsed in blender) for pine nuts. Substituted dried dates (cut into raisin sizes then soaked in water to remove excess sweetness. I drank the water it soaked in so I didn't feel wasteful). And I doubled all measurements for the spices. Amazing and easy with plenty of leftovers!

Excellent recipe, easy and tasty. A nice savory breakfast dish as well as a side. I use more garlic (3 cloves instead of 1), and I prefer it without the garbanzo beans. Also, I use golden raisins which means you can skip the soaking, as long as they’re plump.

Yum. I substituted a mix of almonds and walnuts for the pine nuts- the grocer didn’t have pine nuts yesterday. Also added more of all spices, as I like my food spicy. This was great. Made a double batch and before adding the nuts, beans and raisins, used the base plus hot Italian sausage to stuff peppers. So good. Will definitely make again.

I did a version of this recipe and it turned out great. I didn't have any cumin, so I substituted paprika and I substituted dried cranberries, for the raisins. I also toasted raw almonds, instead of the pine nuts at 350 for about 10 minutes. Explosion of flavors!! It was more delish then I ever expected. Thanks.

This was delightfully delicious!! The flavor is prominent but not overpowering which creates a really tasty dish. I made some minor changes (substituted bullion, craisins and toasted slivered almonds and cut down the curry by 1/2tsp) but otherwise stayed true to the overall recipe. I served this as a salad so I also added a chopped orange pepper. Also, as others have stated, the raisins (or in my case craisins) are essential in giving this dish the pop of sweetness it needs so do not omit them. If you do, it changes the entire taste of this dish. Instead of plumping my craisins separately, I tossed them into the pot of cooking quinoa for the last few minutes. my hubby, who does not "do" anything remotely exotic really enjoyed this dish too! Will be making again :-)

This is an excellent base recipe and leaves so many options open for adaptation. My only specific change from what is written is to leave out the cinnamon. Personally not a fan of cinnamon with curry. My adaptions, first double the recipe. Shredded a couple of carrots into the onion and garlic saute. Left out the cinnamon. Use one can of chickpeas and roughly the equivalent of regular peas - saute/toast them in a pan together before adding. Used almonds instead of pine nuts. Definitely include the raisins. LOTS of flavor.

This recipe has the potential to be really good, but it is a little sloppily put together. The amount of broth is way too much for the cooking time. It definitely needs to be reduced or the cooking time extended. The flavors blend well, in my opinion. Definitely omitted the raisins for personal taste issue. I used a mix of pine nuts and cashews for the nuts, which worked well. Also upped the garlic content after reading reviews about overwhelming curry flavor. Will try again with reduced stock.
TASTES GREAT! I used Black Beans vs Chick Peas, added more garlic, diced carrot and green onion too…

Great meal! I doubled the recipe for a main dish for my family of 5. I added pieced chicken thighs that I had pan fried at the end to sit in the mix for a bit. I used only one serving of beans because I had the chicken and didn't want to overwhelm the dish. The flavors are great and we will make it again!

Loved it. It's suggestive of Biryani, but with quinoa instead of rice. I omitted the pine nuts and chopped pecans instead, and added a pinch of turmeric and garam masala. Quite nice. I should also add that your experience with the curry powder you choose will be different--as "curry" powder is essentially a unique combination of different spices, and each person or each company that produces such mixed powders, will have a slightly different composition (think of seasoned salt, with its common core ingredients, but special variations). I tried this recipe once with Sun Brand Madras Curry powder (coriander seeds, turmeric, chili, salt, cumin seeds, fennel seeds, cinnamon, cloves, anise and mustard), and once with Rani Brand Hot Curry Powder (Coriander, turmeric, Cumin, Mustard, Fenugreek, Black Pepper, Garlic, Fennel, Poppy Seeds, chili and dried curry leaves). I also did it a third time, using my own hand-mixed curry powder (turmeric, red chili powder, garlic, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, cinnamon), plus fresh chopped cilantro. So, you can see how greatly the result would be affected by your choice in curry powder mix, or hand mix.
Wow this was so delicious! I will be making this again
Delicious! Added twice amount of spices as called for. Family enjoyed and I will make again. So easy!

Great base recipe with lots of room for play. I didn’t have pine nuts or raisins (I live on a sailboat without access to stores), so I tried it with raisins and corn and it was delicious. It is an interesting mix of sweet and savory. I added some extra madras curry powder and garam masala instead of cinnamon. Yum!

I made it according to the recipe except the pine nuts (was afraid to try them after hearing that some experience a metallic taste for weeks after eating). It's really good, but next time I am going to skip the Garbanzo beans as I don't really care for the gritty texture. But the recipe is easy to make and very good.
Truly delicious. I like to try a new recipe exactly as described, usually, but today I had no pine nuts, so I sliced some almonds roughly to provide texture and that worked well.

This was sooo good! Served as a side to grilled salmon and a perfect pairing. Simple seasoning that packs a punch. Texture is amazing, grain plus whole chick peas plus tiny pine nuts plus the winner... (I used golden bc I find them to be juicier, no need to soak) raisins! Yum! All kids, husband and dinner guest loved this side.
My family loved it. We enjoy the taste of curry. The leftovers are great on a bed of romaine for a lunch salad.
This is quite good! Though, I would add more Raisons and stir in some coconut before serving and, perhaps some banana. I served it with broiled Alaskan cod.
I have made this dish many times. It freezes well to take for my lunch.
